verdict.label: Light review
verdict.summary: Strava API app setup is self-serve up to 10 users but requires an active Strava subscription, with manual approval required for higher rate limits or capacity.

composioFit.summary: Strava is not available as a Composio managed app, so developers must register their own app on Strava and configure custom OAuth credentials in Composio.
whyOwnApp: Strava is not included in Composio's catalog of managed OAuth toolkits.
Custom OAuth app is required to define callback domains and receive dedicated rate limit quotas.
Granular control over activity read and write scopes is required for your specific application.

phases.name: Register Strava Application
steps: Sign up or log in at https://www.strava.com/register with an active subscription.
Fill in Application Name, Category, Club, Website, and Authorization Callback Domain.
Save and retrieve your Client ID and Client Secret.
phases.handoff: Obtain Client ID and Client Secret to configure Composio auth.

phases.name: Configure Auth Config in Composio
steps: Open Composio Dashboard and navigate to Auth Configs.
Select Create Auth Config and choose OAuth2.
Enter the Strava Client ID and Client Secret.
Ensure the callback URI from Composio matches the Authorization Callback Domain in Strava.
phases.handoff: Auth config created; ready to initiate OAuth login flow for dev users.

phases.name: Test Developer Integration
steps: Initiate authorization via GET https://www.strava.com/oauth/authorize with your client_id and required scopes.
Authorize the app with your own athlete account.
Exchange authorization code for refresh and access tokens via POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token.
phases.handoff: Initial authorization successful for dev testing up to 10 users.

phases.name: Request Capacity Increase & App Review
steps: Submit request to increase rate limits or athlete capacity beyond 10 registered users.
Wait for Strava developer support review.
phases.handoff: Strava notifies developer upon approval for expanded tier.

artefacts.title: Strava API Application Registration Values
artefacts.body:
Application Name: AI Agent Assistant
Category: Mobile App / Helper Agent
Club: N/A
Website: https://yourapp.example.com
Application Description: AI agent integration for tracking athlete activity data and workouts via Composio.
Authorization Callback Domain: <Composio callback URL host from your auth config>

artefacts.title: Strava OAuth Scopes Justification
artefacts.body:
Requested Scopes:
- activity:read: Required to fetch public and follower activity data for the athlete.
- activity:read_all: Required to access athlete private activities and privacy zone details for complete context.
- activity:write: Required to create manual workout activities and upload fitness metrics on behalf of the athlete.

requirements.label: Active Strava Subscription
requirements.when: Required when creating an API app at https://www.strava.com/settings/api

requirements.label: 10-Athlete Limit for Standard Early Development
requirements.when: Standard Tier apps are limited to 10 registered users initially until expanded or reviewed

scopes.purpose: Read user activity data visible to Everyone and Followers, excluding privacy zones
Read user activity data including privacy zones and 'Only You' visibility activities
Create manual activities/uploads and edit activities visible to the app

redirectRules.rule: The Authorization Callback Domain in Strava settings must match the hostname of the redirect_uri supplied in OAuth requests (e.g., localhost for development or your custom app domain).

blockers.cause: The client_id provided in the authorization request URL does not exist or is invalid.
blockers.fix: Copy the exact Client ID generated on https://www.strava.com/settings/api into your auth config.
blockers.fallback: Verify app creation status at https://www.strava.com/settings/api.

blockers.symptom: Unable to create API application at https://www.strava.com/settings/api
blockers.cause: Strava requires an active paid Strava subscription to register and manage API apps.
blockers.fix: Ensure the account creating the application has an active Strava subscription.
blockers.fallback: Subscribe to Strava before setting up the API application.

checklist.text: Ensure account has an active Strava subscription.
Copy Client ID and Client Secret from Strava settings page.
Set Authorization Callback Domain in Strava settings to match Composio callback domain.
Create custom OAuth2 auth config in Composio Dashboard using Strava credentials.
Execute initial user authorization test and exchange code via POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token.
Implement webhooks for handling athlete deauthorization events as required by API terms.

uncertainties: Exact processing time for athlete capacity increase requests, as Strava explicitly does not provide a fixed SLA.

claims.text: All developers must register an application to receive a client ID and client secret before initiating OAuth.
claims.quote: All developers need to register their application before getting started. A registered application will be assigned a client ID and client secret.

claims.text: Creating an API application on Strava requires an active Strava subscription.
claims.quote: After you are logged in, go to https://www.strava.com/settings/api and create an app. Note: A Strava subscription is required.

claims.text: Strava apps require specifying an Authorization Callback Domain, set to localhost or a domain.
claims.quote: Authorization Callback Domain: When building your app, change “Authorization Callback Domain” to localhost or any domain. When taking your app live, change “Authorization Callback Domain” to a real do

claims.text: Default Strava API rate limits allow 200 requests every 15 minutes up to 2,000 requests per day.
claims.quote: The default rate limit allows 200 requests every 15 minutes, with up to 2,000 requests per day.

claims.text: Scope activity:read allows reading user activity data visible to Everyone and Followers.
claims.quote: - activity:read : read the user's activity data for activities that are visible to Everyone and Followers, excluding privacy zone data

claims.text: Scope activity:read_all grants access to activity:read plus privacy zone data and 'Only You' activities.
claims.quote: - activity:read_all : the same access as activity:read , plus privacy zone data and access to read the user's activities with visibility set to Only You

claims.text: Scope activity:write grants access to create manual activities and uploads, and edit visible activities.
claims.quote: - activity:write : access to create manual activities and uploads, and access to edit any activities that are visible to the app, based on activity read access level

claims.text: Standard Tier apps are initially limited to 10 registered Strava users for hobbyists and early development.
claims.quote: (a) Standard Tier (“Standard Tier Applications”), inclusive of two levels: - Developer Applications limited to 10 registered Strava users (generally intended for hobbyists, side projects, and early de

claims.text: Standard Tier applications can be limited to 9,999 registered Strava users for growing apps.
claims.quote: Developer Applications limited to 9,999 registered Strava users (generally intended for growing apps with a substantial user base);

claims.text: Strava does not commit to a fixed review-time SLA for developer admission or capacity increase requests.
claims.quote: Strava does not commit to a fixed review-time service-level agreement; you will hear from Strava if you are admitted, or if Strava requires additional information.

claims.text: Applications exchange authorization codes for access and refresh tokens via POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token.
claims.quote: The application must now call the POST https://www.strava.com/oauth/token with its client ID and client secret to exchange the authorization code for a refresh token and short-lived access token.

claims.text: Developers are required to implement webhooks to handle athlete deauthorization events.
claims.quote: Per our API terms, you need to implement webhooks to know when an athlete has deauthorized your API application

claims.text: Strava is not present in Composio's managed toolkit catalog, requiring custom auth configuration.
claims.artifact: lookup:composio-directory (Strava not among 387 OAuth toolkits on docs.composio.dev/toolkits/managed-auth)

claims.text: For custom OAuth toolkits, developers register an app in the provider portal and add credentials to Composio.
claims.quote: For OAuth toolkits, register an app in the provider's developer portal and add the redirect URI from the dashboard. Then copy the Client ID and Client Secret back into Composio.

claims.text: Strava MCP is the official interface for personal AI use and cannot be used for third-party access.
claims.quote: The Strava MCP is not authorized for, and may not be used to enable, any commercial or third-party access to the Strava API Materials or Strava Data outside the developer's own personal use.

claims.text: Requesting authorization with an invalid client_id returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with field client_id code invalid.
